evidence.claim: Kelleher completed a permanent transfer from Liverpool to Brentford in summer 2025 for an initial fee reported at £12.5m rising to £18m, signing a five-year contract, after stating he wanted "to be a number one and to play every week."
evidence.interpretation: A move motivated explicitly by seeking regular first-team football suggests the player prioritised playing time over staying at a bigger club, which is a positive precursor to on-field development.

evidence.claim: Kelleher started all 37 Premier League matches for Brentford in 2025-26, keeping 10 clean sheets, after making only 10 Premier League appearances for Liverpool in the whole of 2024-25.
evidence.interpretation: A jump from a small number of appearances as a backup to a full season as an undisputed starting goalkeeper is strong evidence of increased playing time and responsibility.

evidence.claim: Travers made only 3 total appearances for Everton in his debut 2025-26 season (2 Carabao Cup starts and a 2-minute late substitute Premier League debut), serving as backup to Jordan Pickford.
evidence.interpretation: A near-total absence of league game time after a permanent transfer indicates a significant drop in playing status compared to his previous role as Bournemouth's first-choice goalkeeper.

evidence.claim: As of August 2026, Coventry City and Wrexham were reported to be interested in signing Travers from Everton, and Middlesbrough were reported to be in talks over a loan deal.
evidence.interpretation: Multiple clubs circling for a move away, combined with minimal 2025-26 game time, suggests Travers is not in Everton's first-team plans and may need to leave to get regular football.
evidence.notes: Unconfirmed whether any of these moves have completed as of 20 August 2026.

evidence.claim: On loan at Leyton Orient in 2024-25, Keeley kept 16 clean sheets in 36 League One games, was named the club's Young Player of the Year, and helped Orient reach the League One play-off final.
evidence.interpretation: A statistically strong loan spell recognised with a club award is solid evidence of a successful development loan ahead of his permanent move.

evidence.claim: Keeley was named in Ireland's 25-man squad for the March 2026 World Cup play-off matches against Czechia, described by RTÉ as his first competitive senior call-up, having previously been called up only for friendlies in June 2025.
evidence.interpretation: Progression from friendly-only call-ups to a competitive squad indicates increasing trust from the national team management, though he remained uncapped as of the last confirmed squad.

evidence.claim: Coleman made only 3 appearances for Everton in the 2025-26 season and announced in May 2026 that he would end his 17-year Everton playing career at the end of that season, having been "ravaged by injuries" and making just 23 appearances over the previous three seasons combined.
evidence.interpretation: A near-total absence from the matchday squad combined with a self-announced end to his playing career is very strong evidence of terminal decline in first-team involvement, not a temporary dip.

evidence.claim: Despite making only 3 club appearances in 2025-26, Coleman was still named in Ireland's 25-man squad for the March 2026 World Cup play-offs and in the squad for the Qatar and Canada friendlies in May/June 2026.
evidence.interpretation: Continued senior call-ups despite minimal club football likely reflect leadership/experience value and squad-building rather than current playing form.

evidence.claim: Collins was named Brentford club captain by manager Keith Andrews ahead of the 2025-26 season, replacing Christian Norgaard who departed to Arsenal, and started 32 of Brentford's 38 Premier League games (35 total appearances, 2,971 minutes, 1 goal, 2 assists).
evidence.interpretation: Being entrusted with the club captaincy and remaining a near-permanent starter is strong evidence of an established, senior role at Premier League level.

evidence.claim: Collins captains the Republic of Ireland national team and had 40 caps and 3 goals as of the most recent figures found (dated around June 2026).
evidence.interpretation: Captaining the national side alongside a Premier League club captaincy indicates a leadership role at both levels.

evidence.claim: Hull City, for whom Egan made 34 appearances (32 starts, 2 goals) in the 2025-26 Championship, beat Middlesbrough 1-0 in the play-off final on 24 May 2026 to win promotion to the Premier League for 2026-27.
evidence.interpretation: Regular starts for a side promoted to the top flight represents a positive development in the level Egan is playing at, moving from Championship to Premier League football at age 33.

evidence.claim: Egan's Hull City contract was extended to June 2027 in January 2026, and as of August 2026 the club is reported to be in advanced talks over a further new contract.
evidence.interpretation: A club moving proactively to extend an ageing defender's contract, even before promotion, indicates he is valued as a key player rather than facing a squad reduction.

evidence.claim: O'Brien made 37 appearances for Everton in the 2025-26 Premier League season, starting 35 times and playing 3,124 minutes, with 1 goal and 1 assist.
evidence.interpretation: A near-full season of starts at centre-back for a Premier League club is strong evidence of an established first-team role.

evidence.claim: O'Shea captained Ipswich Town to a 46-appearance, 4,140-minute season in the 2025-26 Championship (1 goal, 1 assist, 292 clearances), as the club finished second and secured an immediate return to the Premier League with a 3-0 win over QPR on the final day.
evidence.interpretation: Ever-present, captaining performances culminating in promotion represent clear positive progression, both in individual playing time and in the level of competition he will face in 2026-27.

evidence.claim: Scales made 37 Scottish Premiership appearances (34 starts) for Celtic in 2025-26, plus 4 Scottish Cup and 9 Europa League appearances, as Celtic won the Scottish Cup; he averaged a 7.1 match rating across the season.
evidence.interpretation: A heavy workload across domestic league, cup and European competition, with a cup winner's medal, indicates a well-established and successful role as a regular starter.

evidence.claim: Bazunu's loan at Stoke City, which began 13 January 2026, was cut short after he made multiple errors across six appearances.
evidence.interpretation: A short, error-marred loan spell that ended early is evidence of a difficult period in his development rather than progression.

evidence.claim: Bazunu ruptured his Achilles tendon in April 2024, then had a loan at Standard Liège (2024-25 season) cut short in April 2025 by a knee/meniscus injury after 8 appearances.
evidence.interpretation: A pattern of serious injuries interrupting successive loan spells is a significant negative factor in his recent development, independent of any assessment of ability.

evidence.claim: Bazunu was not named in either the 25-man March 2026 World Cup play-off squad or the 24-man May 2026 Qatar/Canada friendly squad, and as of 19 August 2026 Southampton were reported to be looking to sell him with Dinamo Zagreb interest reported.
evidence.interpretation: Absence from two consecutive senior squads combined with a club looking to sell him suggests he has fallen well down the pecking order both for his club and country.

evidence.claim: Ligue1.com described Omobamidele's spell at Strasbourg as a "rebirth" restoring a player who had become "Ireland's forgotten defender", noting a run of 7 consecutive Ligue 1 starts and Strasbourg's run to the UEFA Conference League semi-finals; he made 25 Ligue 1 appearances in 2025-26 with 1,350 minutes, 1 goal and 7 clean sheets in matches he played.
evidence.interpretation: A named turnaround narrative from a reputable competition-affiliated outlet, backed by a run of consecutive starts, is evidence of improved form and playing time after a difficult spell at Nottingham Forest.

evidence.claim: Omobamidele was not named in the 25-man March 2026 World Cup play-off squad or the 24-man May 2026 Qatar/Canada friendly squad, despite the positive club-level reporting on his form at Strasbourg.
evidence.interpretation: Absence from two consecutive senior squads despite improved club form suggests he was not currently part of the national team management's plans, independent of his club performance.

evidence.claim: Heffernan signed permanently for National League club Harrogate Town from Newcastle United on 14 January 2026, on an 18-month deal, having previously captained Newcastle's U21 side (19 appearances, 3 goals in 2025-26 before the move).
evidence.interpretation: A move from a Premier League club's U21 setup to a fifth-tier senior club represents a drop in the level of football, though it also represents a move toward regular senior first-team football rather than continued age-group football.

evidence.claim: Ryan Manning made 45 appearances, starting 37, and scored 8 goals for Southampton in the Championship in 2025-26.
evidence.interpretation: A near-full season of regular starts and a notably high goal return for a full-back suggests a strong, undiminished role in his club's team.
evidence.notes: Figures drawn from a statistics aggregator rather than an official club or league source; not independently cross-checked against a second source.

evidence.claim: Manning was withdrawn from Ireland's squad ahead of the May 2026 friendlies against Qatar and Canada.
evidence.interpretation: A late withdrawal from a national squad, alongside a club teammate, points to a fitness issue rather than a loss of favour with the manager.
evidence.notes: Exact injury type not stated in the source found.

evidence.claim: Jayson Molumby was named in both the 25-man March 2026 World Cup play-off squad and the 24-man May 2026 Qatar/Canada friendlies squad.
evidence.interpretation: Consistent selection across both squads indicates he remained a first-choice senior midfielder through this period.

evidence.claim: Molumby made 38 appearances (31 starts) for West Bromwich Albion in the 2025-26 Championship season, totalling 2,902 minutes with 2 goals and 2 assists.
evidence.interpretation: A high volume of starts across the season shows he remained a first-choice club midfielder.

evidence.claim: Alan Browne spent the 2025-26 season on loan at Middlesbrough from Sunderland, making 23 appearances (13 starts) and scoring once, then returned to Sunderland for 2026-27 with no permanent move confirmed.
evidence.interpretation: A loan spell followed by a return to the parent club without a permanent deal suggests an unresolved, potentially unstable club situation heading into 2026-27.
evidence.notes: Two sources gave differing appearance/start splits for the loan spell (23 apps/13 starts vs 19 starts/16 other appearances); both recorded in the player entry.

evidence.claim: Browne was ruled out of Ireland's May 2026 Qatar/Canada squad through injury, having been part of the March 2026 play-off squad.
evidence.interpretation: Missing a squad through injury after being a regular selection is a short-term interruption rather than necessarily a loss of the manager's confidence.

evidence.claim: Jack Taylor made 25 appearances (24 starts), scoring twice with one assist, for Ipswich Town in the 2025-26 Championship season, and signed a new three-year contract with the club.
evidence.interpretation: Regular starts plus a fresh long-term contract suggest he is an established, valued first-team player at club level.

evidence.claim: Taylor was named in the March 2026 play-off squad but not in the May 2026 Qatar/Canada squad.
evidence.interpretation: Absence from a squad following inclusion in the previous one may reflect rotation for a friendly window rather than a longer-term drop, but no explicit reason was found.

evidence.claim: Jason Knight had 41 caps and 1 goal for Ireland as of November 2025, having debuted against Finland on 14 October 2020, and was named in the March 2026 play-off squad but not the May 2026 squad.
evidence.interpretation: A high caps total shows established senior status, while absence from the following squad is a data point to watch rather than confirmed evidence of a change in status.

evidence.claim: Finn Azaz transferred from Middlesbrough to Southampton on 29 August 2025 on a four-year deal, having recorded 17 goals and 17 assists in 67 league games for Middlesbrough.
evidence.interpretation: A significant goal/assist output prompting a move within the Championship reflects strong prior club form, though it is a lateral rather than clearly upward league move.

evidence.claim: Azaz withdrew from Ireland's May 2026 squad for the Qatar and Canada friendlies alongside Southampton teammate Ryan Manning.
evidence.interpretation: A withdrawal alongside a club colleague around the same time raises the possibility of a shared club-related fitness issue, though this is not confirmed.

evidence.claim: Robbie Brady made only 5 league appearances for Preston North End in the 2025-26 season, first appearing in February 2026 after an injury-disrupted campaign, and was released when Preston did not extend his contract.
evidence.interpretation: A severely reduced appearance count followed by release is strong evidence of declining first-team involvement at club level.

evidence.claim: Brady was named in the March 2026 World Cup play-off squad but not in the May 2026 Qatar/Canada squad, and remained without a club as of the most recent reporting found (19 May 2026).
evidence.interpretation: Being without a club shortly after a senior squad inclusion suggests his international involvement may be at risk if he cannot secure regular club football.

evidence.claim: Jamie McGrath was named Hibernian's Player of the Year for the 2025-26 season, his debut campaign at the club, recording 41 appearances and 13 goal involvements (32 league appearances, 8 league goals, 4 assists).
evidence.interpretation: Winning a club's top individual award in a debut season is strong evidence of a successful move and high-level performance.

evidence.claim: McGrath was named in the May 2026 Qatar/Canada squad but not the March 2026 play-off squad.
evidence.interpretation: Inclusion following a standout club season is consistent with strong form translating into international selection.

evidence.claim: Killian Phillips scored twice on the opening day of the 2026-27 Scottish Premiership season against Falkirk and was named SPFL Premiership Team of the Week 'Star Man', then scored again from the penalty spot against St Johnstone; his St Mirren contract was extended to 2027.
evidence.interpretation: Strong opening-weeks form and a contract extension point to an upward trajectory at club level, though this falls in the new 2026-27 season with very limited sample size.

evidence.claim: Phillips was named in the May 2026 Qatar/Canada squad but not the March 2026 play-off squad.
evidence.interpretation: First appearance in a senior squad list found in this research; consistent with a breakthrough into senior international contention.

evidence.claim: Joe Hodge moved from CD Tondela (Portugal) to Motherwell in Scotland in August 2026, on a two-year deal with a club option for a further year, after a transfer that nearly collapsed over a Wolves sell-on clause dispute.
evidence.interpretation: A move to a more familiar football culture/league after one season abroad could support settled, regular first-team football, but the transfer's troubled process is worth noting.

evidence.claim: Hodge was named in the May 2026 Qatar/Canada squad as one of five players receiving a first senior Ireland call-up, having previously captained the Ireland U21 side.
evidence.interpretation: A first senior call-up following U21 captaincy is a clear breakthrough marker.
evidence.notes: A separate secondary source described Hodge's senior debut as coming in a June friendly draw with Canada in Montreal, which is broadly consistent with the fixture list, but the exact chronology of 'first call-up' versus 'debut' across sources was not fully reconciled.

evidence.claim: Conor Coventry received his first senior Ireland call-up in autumn 2025 (Armenia qualifier, then Portugal and Hungary qualifiers in November), and was named in the May 2026 squad for the Canada leg of the Qatar/Canada friendlies.
evidence.interpretation: Progression from Ireland's all-time U21 appearance record holder into senior squads is clear evidence of underage-to-senior progression.

evidence.claim: Coventry made 40 appearances (33 starts) for Charlton Athletic in the 2025-26 Championship season.
evidence.interpretation: A high number of starts across a Championship season shows he was a regular, trusted first-team player at club level.

evidence.claim: Dawson Devoy, Bohemians' captain, was named in the May 2026 squad for the Canada leg of the Qatar/Canada friendlies, one of four League of Ireland players included, with reporting noting he was aiming to become the first Bohemians player capped at senior level by Ireland since Glen Crowe in 2002.
evidence.interpretation: A first call-up for a League of Ireland captain is significant breakthrough evidence, though it is not confirmed here whether he actually earned a cap by playing.

evidence.claim: Corrie Ndaba received his first senior Ireland call-up and made his senior debut in May 2026, after moving from Kilmarnock to Lecce in Serie A in summer 2025 and making his Serie A debut in September 2025.
evidence.interpretation: A move to a top-five European league followed swiftly by a first senior international call-up is strong evidence of rising stock.

evidence.claim: Andrew Omobamidele suffered recurring ankle injuries during the 2025-26 season at Strasbourg, including one sustained just before half-time in a 1-0 win over Nantes, and was ruled out of Ireland's May 2026 Qatar/Canada squad through injury.
evidence.interpretation: Repeated injury setbacks across a season, culminating in missing an international squad, is evidence of a disrupted season limiting his availability and progression.

evidence.claim: Omobamidele's loan move to Strasbourg was made permanent on 24 June 2025, on a contract until 2029.
evidence.interpretation: Securing a permanent move and a long contract at a Ligue 1 club, despite subsequent injury issues, indicates the club retained confidence in him.
evidence.notes: Wikipedia used only to locate/corroborate; the underlying permanent-transfer fact is consistent with the Get French Football News reporting on his subsequent injury, which independently identifies him as a Strasbourg player under contract.

evidence.claim: Sam Curtis joined League Two club Chesterfield on loan from Sheffield United (confirmed 4 January 2026) and scored on his debut in a 2-2 draw against MK Dons.
evidence.interpretation: An immediate goal-scoring debut on a new loan suggests a positive start to gaining first-team experience outside his parent club.

evidence.claim: Andrew Moran joined Preston North End on a three-and-a-half-year deal in February 2026, making 11 appearances afterward as the club finished 14th in the Championship.
evidence.interpretation: A long-term contract signing suggests the club's confidence in him, though a mid-table finish and limited appearance count are modest evidence of impact.

evidence.claim: Rocco Vata started 10 of Watford's first 13 Championship matches in 2025-26 before a hamstring injury in November 2025 sidelined him, and he was not included in the confirmed March or May 2026 Ireland squads.
evidence.interpretation: A strong early-season run of starts followed by a long-term injury and subsequent absence from squads suggests his season, and international involvement, was significantly disrupted.

evidence.claim: Mark McGuinness moved from Cardiff City to Sheffield United after making 56 competitive appearances and scoring 3 goals for Cardiff.
evidence.interpretation: A transfer following a substantial run of appearances at his previous club suggests continued opportunity, though the destination club's league level relative to Cardiff was not independently confirmed as an upward move.

evidence.claim: Troy Parrott (AZ Alkmaar) was named in Heimir Hallgrímsson's 25-man Republic of Ireland squad for the March 2026 World Cup play-off matches against Czechia and Denmark/North Macedonia.
evidence.interpretation: Confirms Parrott's continued status as a first-choice senior international striker at the time of Ireland's most recent competitive fixtures.

evidence.claim: Parrott was reported as AZ Alkmaar's top Eredivisie goalscorer with 15 league goals in the 2025-26 season.
evidence.interpretation: If accurate, this suggests a strong scoring season at a reasonably competitive European league level, though the figure comes from aggregated secondary sources rather than a directly fetched primary statistics page.
evidence.notes: Not independently verified against a primary stats provider (e.g. Eredivisie official site) due to tool access limitations; flagged in player's unverified list.

evidence.claim: Adam Idah moved permanently from Celtic (Scottish Premiership) to Swansea City (EFL Championship) for a reported fee of £6m, completed 1 September 2025, signing a five-year contract.
evidence.interpretation: A move from limited Celtic first-team football to a starting Championship role represents an increase in regular game time, though the leagues are of broadly comparable standard rather than a clear step up or down.

evidence.claim: Idah made only two league appearances for Celtic in 2025-26 before his September 2025 move, then made 25 league appearances and scored 6 goals for Swansea City that season.
evidence.interpretation: A substantial increase in playing time following the transfer, consistent with a more prominent first-team role at Swansea.

evidence.claim: Idah was passed fit and named in Ireland's squad for the March 2026 World Cup play-offs after a fitness concern.
evidence.interpretation: Confirms he remained part of the senior squad despite a fitness question in the build-up.

evidence.claim: Szmodics received a recall to Ireland's March 2026 play-off squad following his loan form at Derby County.
evidence.interpretation: Suggests his club form directly influenced his return to the senior squad.

evidence.claim: Szmodics does not appear in the FAI's squad list for the May/June 2026 Qatar and Canada friendlies.
evidence.interpretation: Indicates a gap in senior involvement between the March play-offs and the May/June friendlies, though no specific reason (form, injury, rest) was found in sources reviewed.
evidence.notes: Absence noted factually; no interpretation beyond squad-list comparison should be over-read given no explicit explanation was found.

evidence.claim: Szmodics re-joined Derby County on a season-long loan from Ipswich Town for 2026-27, with an obligation for Derby to buy him (fee dependent on promotion), having scored 3 goals and 1 assist in a first loan spell there in the second half of 2025-26.
evidence.interpretation: A repeated loan with a buy obligation suggests both clubs see him as a regular contributor at Championship level, though it also means he remains outside Ipswich's Premier League/Championship first-team plans.

evidence.claim: Ogbene made 10 starts and 3 substitute appearances (1 goal, 1 assist) while on loan at Sheffield United in the 2025-26 Championship season.
evidence.interpretation: A modest goal/assist return in a squad role rather than an undisputed starting one, at Championship level.

evidence.claim: Ogbene was named in Ireland's squads for both the March 2026 World Cup play-offs (while on loan at Sheffield United) and the May/June 2026 Qatar and Canada friendlies (listed at parent club Ipswich Town).
evidence.interpretation: Indicates continued senior selection across both windows regardless of loan/parent-club status.

evidence.claim: Kenny scored 6 goals and added 3 assists in 14 appearances during a loan at Bolton Wanderers in the second half of 2025-26, helping the club to promotion via the play-offs.
evidence.interpretation: A strong scoring rate in a short loan spell, and direct involvement in a promotion, is positive evidence of a successful loan.

evidence.claim: A proposed permanent transfer of Kenny to Bolton Wanderers did not go through in summer 2026; Celtic confirmed he would remain at the club for 2026-27 to compete with new signings including Kasper Høgh.
evidence.interpretation: Staying at Celtic despite a promising loan suggests he will need to compete for first-team minutes against new signings rather than guaranteed a starting role.

evidence.claim: Kenny was named in Ireland's 25-man squad for the March 2026 World Cup play-offs while on loan at Bolton Wanderers.
evidence.interpretation: Confirms senior involvement driven by loan form.

evidence.claim: Mason Melia received his first senior Ireland call-up for the May/June 2026 Qatar and Canada friendlies, described as being 'fast-tracked' into the squad, and earned 2 caps (v Qatar and v Canada).
evidence.interpretation: An unusually rapid path to senior international football for an 18-year-old who had only just left the League of Ireland, reflecting the coaching staff's confidence in his potential rather than an established club track record.

evidence.claim: Melia was loaned from Tottenham Hotspur to Lincoln City in the EFL Championship for the 2026-27 season, confirmed 5 August 2026, having not yet made a competitive first-team appearance for Spurs.
evidence.interpretation: A loan to a newly promoted Championship side is a standard development pathway for a young forward who is yet to break into a Premier League first team, rather than evidence of regression.

evidence.claim: Melia transferred from St Patrick's Athletic to Tottenham Hotspur on 1 January 2026 for a reported record fee for a League of Ireland player.
evidence.interpretation: A significant step up in level from League of Ireland football to a Premier League academy/first-team environment.

evidence.claim: Ferguson was ruled out of the March 2026 World Cup play-offs while awaiting ankle surgery, having missed his last seven Serie A matches for loan club AS Roma; he underwent surgery in the UK in spring 2026, expected to end his 2025-26 season.
evidence.interpretation: A significant injury setback that removed him from senior international contention for the most consequential fixtures of the qualifying campaign.

evidence.claim: Ferguson's loan at AS Roma is reported as 'likely over' following the surgery decision, with Roma considered unlikely to activate any buy option in the loan agreement with Brighton.
evidence.interpretation: Despite scoring 5 goals in 22 games before the injury recurred, the loan appears set to end without a permanent move, reducing his settled first-team options ahead of 2026-27.

evidence.claim: Ebosele transferred from İstanbul Başakşehir to newly promoted Süper Lig club Erzurumspor for an undisclosed fee, confirmed 9 August 2026, reportedly to become the club's first-choice right-back.
evidence.interpretation: A lateral move within the same league, reportedly aimed at securing more regular playing time rather than a step up or down in level.

evidence.claim: Ebosele was not included in either the March or May/June 2026 Republic of Ireland senior squads identified in this research.
evidence.interpretation: No specific reason for the absence was found in sources reviewed; as a right-back/wing-back rather than a forward or winger, his omission may reflect a different positional pecking order rather than form or injury, but this is not confirmed.
evidence.notes: Absence noted factually only; no reliable source found explaining the specific reason.

evidence.claim: Johnston made 34 first-team appearances for West Bromwich Albion in the 2025-26 season but was not included in either the March or May/June 2026 Ireland senior squads identified in this research.
evidence.interpretation: Regular club minutes did not translate into senior international selection during this window; no specific reason was found in sources reviewed, so this should not be read as evidence of a coaching decision without further confirmation.

evidence.claim: McAteer transferred permanently from Leicester City to Ipswich Town in August 2025 on a four-year contract, having made 18 Premier League appearances for Leicester in 2024-25.
evidence.interpretation: A move between clubs at a similar level (both aiming for/around the Premier League-Championship boundary), rather than a clear rise or fall in level.

evidence.claim: McAteer, who has 8 senior Ireland caps as of November 2025, was not included in either the March or May/June 2026 senior squads identified in this research.
evidence.interpretation: A gap in senior selection following an initial run of caps; no specific reason was found in sources reviewed.

evidence.claim: After joining Sheffield United permanently for a reported ~£10m fee in January 2025, Cannon scored 7 goals in 54 appearances across all competitions through the 2025-26 season, having scored 11 goals in 25 appearances during a prior loan spell at Stoke City.
evidence.interpretation: A lower goals-per-appearance rate at Sheffield United compared with his Stoke loan spell, though appearance totals combine multiple competitions and are not broken out by competition.

evidence.claim: Cannon was not included in either the March or May/June 2026 Ireland senior squads identified in this research, despite remaining a regular contributor at Sheffield United.
evidence.interpretation: No specific reason was found in sources reviewed for this absence.

evidence.claim: Zefi signed for League of Ireland Premier Division club Sligo Rovers as a free agent in late May 2026, having left AS Roma, where he had been 'blighted with injury' and had not made a first-team breakthrough after moving there from Inter Milan.
evidence.interpretation: A significant drop in level from a big-five European league academy to League of Ireland football, consistent with a stalled development pathway rather than a rise.

evidence.claim: Zefi has been capped by Ireland at U15, U17 and U19 level and made his U21 debut against Sweden in 2024, having previously scored 19 goals in 19 appearances for Inter Milan's U18 side.
evidence.interpretation: Strong underage statistical output at Inter Milan did not translate into a first-team career at either Inter or Roma, illustrating the gap between academy scoring records and senior breakthrough.

evidence.claim: O'Neill has 13 caps and 2 goals for the Republic of Ireland U21 team, including a 92nd-minute winner against Sweden on 17 November 2021, and plays for Leyton Orient in EFL League One.
evidence.interpretation: Consistent underage international involvement, but no evidence found of a senior call-up as of August 2026.

evidence.claim: Emakhu transferred from Millwall to Oxford United on a long-term deal in February 2026, having made 27 Championship appearances (2 goals, 1 assist) combined across the season.
evidence.interpretation: A mid-season move within the same division (Championship), suggesting a change of environment rather than a clear rise or fall in level.

evidence.claim: Armstrong transferred permanently from Bristol City to Turkish Süper Lig club Göztepe for a reported fee of around £2.1-2.16m, confirmed mid-June 2026, on a four-year contract with a 12-month option.
evidence.interpretation: A move to a different European top-tier league; whether this represents a stronger or weaker league is not clear-cut and is not asserted either way here.

evidence.claim: Armstrong has one senior Ireland cap, won in a defeat to the Netherlands in September 2023, and was recalled to a squad for a Nations League play-off against Bulgaria in March 2025, but was not part of either the March or May/June 2026 senior squads identified in this research.
evidence.interpretation: A single cap followed by a lengthy gap in senior selection suggests he has not established a consistent place in the senior squad, though no specific reason for the 2026 omissions was found.

evidence.claim: Robinson last played for Ireland in September 2024 (6 minutes v Greece in the Nations League) and had not been called up again as of the most recent reporting found (September 2025); he was not included in either the March or May/June 2026 senior squads identified in this research.
evidence.interpretation: A lengthy absence from senior selection stretching back nearly two years, though no specific reason (form, coaching decision, or other) was found in sources reviewed.

evidence.claim: Robinson's club, Cardiff City, was relegated from the Championship to League One at the end of the 2024-25 season despite Robinson being the club's top scorer (12 goals in 35 appearances) and Player of the Season.
evidence.interpretation: A drop to a lower division for his club, though this reflects team results rather than Robinson's individual performance, which was reported as strong that season.

evidence.claim: Johansson won a FIFA-cleared switch of international allegiance from Luxembourg to the Republic of Ireland in May 2021, having previously represented Luxembourg and Sweden at youth level.
evidence.interpretation: Confirms his Ireland eligibility is settled and no longer contested, though this predates the period covered by this research.

evidence.claim: Johansson made 13 appearances (1 goal) in Germany's 3. Liga for SV Wehen Wiesbaden in the 2025-26 season, at a club playing in the third tier of German football.
evidence.interpretation: Limited statistical output at third-tier level with no evidence found of senior Ireland involvement, consistent with u21/emerging rather than senior status.

evidence.claim: Sam Curtis made 24 appearances in all competitions for Chesterfield during a 2025-26 loan spell from Sheffield United.
evidence.interpretation: A high appearance count on loan at League Two level suggests he was a regular starter and gaining first-team experience below Championship level, though it also indicates he was not yet ready for regular Championship football.

evidence.claim: Sam Curtis was named in the Republic of Ireland U21 squad announced by the FAI on 1 June 2026 for friendlies against Croatia U21 and Qatar U23.
evidence.interpretation: Continued inclusion in U21 squads shows he remains part of the age-grade international pathway, though squad inclusion alone does not confirm he played.

evidence.claim: James Abankwah received his first Republic of Ireland senior call-up ahead of the March 2025 UEFA Nations League play-off against Bulgaria, and was named in the FAI's 5 May 2026 squad for the Grenada friendly.
evidence.interpretation: Sustained senior selection over more than a year, including a call-up necessitated partly by injuries to established defenders, indicates he has established himself as a senior squad option rather than a one-off inclusion.

evidence.claim: James Abankwah made 19 Championship appearances (17 starts) on loan at Watford in 2024-25 and signed a further season-long loan at Watford for 2025-26.
evidence.interpretation: A high starts-to-appearances ratio and a repeat loan by the same club suggest the parent club (Udinese) and Watford both view him as a regular contributor rather than a fringe squad player.

evidence.claim: Jaden Umeh made his Republic of Ireland senior debut as a substitute on 28 May 2026 against Qatar, then made his first senior start on 5 June 2026 against Canada, playing 70 minutes, aged 18.
evidence.interpretation: Progressing from a substitute cameo to a full 70-minute start within the same international window, at 18 years old, is a fast and clear breakthrough into senior international football.

evidence.claim: Jaden Umeh was fast-tracked into Benfica's first-team picture by manager José Mourinho, according to Irish Examiner reporting (headline only; article was inaccessible in this session).
evidence.interpretation: If accurate, first-team involvement at a major European club alongside senior international recognition would indicate rapid dual progression at club and country level, but this claim rests on a headline only since the article could not be fetched.
evidence.notes: Article access was denied in this research session; claim is based on the search-result headline/summary only, not a fetched article body.

evidence.claim: Rocco Vata received his first Republic of Ireland senior call-up for the March 2025 Nations League play-off against Bulgaria and made his debut as a 79th-minute substitute in a 2-1 first-leg win in Plovdiv.
evidence.interpretation: A senior debut off the bench in a high-stakes play-off match indicates the coaching staff trusted him in a pressure situation despite limited senior experience.

evidence.claim: Rocco Vata transferred from Celtic (Scottish Premiership) to Watford (EFL Championship) prior to his March 2025 Ireland call-up, recording three goals and three assists for Watford that season.
evidence.interpretation: Regular attacking output in a new league in the same season as a senior call-up supports the idea the move helped his international prospects, though league level comparisons between the Scottish Premiership and Championship are not straightforward.

evidence.claim: Trent Kone-Doherty left Liverpool for Norwegian club Molde FK in a permanent transfer worth a reported €750,000, completed 27 February 2026, with Liverpool retaining buyback and sell-on clauses.
evidence.interpretation: A move from a Premier League academy to a Norwegian top-flight club is a step down in league prestige but likely represents a route to regular senior first-team football that was not being offered at Liverpool.

evidence.claim: Trent Kone-Doherty made two senior appearances for Liverpool in cup competitions (FA Cup at Plymouth Argyle, February 2025; Carabao Cup vs Crystal Palace) before setting a Liverpool record for UEFA Youth League appearances in early 2026.
evidence.interpretation: Fringe senior cup involvement combined with heavy youth-competition use suggests he was highly regarded within the academy but not settled as a first-team squad member, consistent with the subsequent permanent transfer.

evidence.claim: Mason Melia earned a Republic of Ireland senior cap in a 1-1 draw with Canada, in the same international window (late May/early June 2026) as Jaden Umeh's senior debut.
evidence.interpretation: A senior cap at 18, while still contracted to Tottenham's development squad, shows unusually rapid international progression relative to his club first-team status at the time.

evidence.claim: After one pre-season substitute appearance for Tottenham's first team (vs Sydney FC, July 2026), Mason Melia was sent on a season-long loan to League One club Lincoln City, announced 5 August 2026.
evidence.interpretation: Being loaned out to English football's third tier after only a single pre-season appearance suggests Tottenham judged he was not yet ready for regular Premier League or even Championship-level first-team football and prioritised game time over first-team proximity.

evidence.claim: Gbemi Arubi signed for EFL League One club Burton Albion from League of Ireland Premier Division club Dundalk in July 2026, on a three-year deal with an option for a further year, after scoring 7 goals in 22 appearances during the 2026 League of Ireland season.
evidence.interpretation: A move from the League of Ireland to English League One, on the back of a productive scoring season, represents a step up in league level typically associated with a player considered ready for a more competitive environment.
evidence.notes: Some sources give slightly different appearance/goal totals (20 apps/6 goals vs 22 apps/7 goals); both are noted in the player record.

evidence.claim: Gbemi Arubi earned his Republic of Ireland U21 debut in a 2-2 draw with Croatia in June 2026.
evidence.interpretation: A first U21 cap alongside a breakout club season and a subsequent move to English football suggests his rise was recognised by both club recruiters and the international set-up in the same window.

evidence.claim: Michael Noonan, aged 17, scored in Shamrock Rovers' 2-0 win over Waterford on 19 June 2026 and was described by RTE as one of the brightest young talents in the country, attracting reported interest from Ajax, Nottingham Forest and Hoffenheim.
evidence.interpretation: Scoring at senior League of Ireland level as a 17-year-old and attracting reported interest from clubs across three countries is suggestive of a genuine breakthrough, though transfer speculation itself is not confirmation of ability and should be treated cautiously.

evidence.claim: Mason Melia's move from St Patrick's Athletic to Tottenham Hotspur in early 2025 was reported as a record fee for a League of Ireland player, with figures reported variously as approximately €1.8m and €2m/£1.75m; he could not officially register until turning 18 on 1 January 2026 under post-Brexit transfer rules.
evidence.interpretation: A record domestic transfer fee reflects strong external assessment of his talent at the point of transfer, independent of subsequent first-team involvement, which per the task instructions should not itself be treated as a measure of ability.
evidence.notes: Fee figures are disputed between sources; both are recorded rather than resolved.

evidence.claim: Tommy Lonergan was reported by WLR FM to be leading the League of Ireland Premier Division Golden Boot race during the 2026 season and won an SSE Airtricity/Soccer Writers Ireland Player of the Month award via a nationwide poll with 50 points.
evidence.interpretation: Leading the top-flight goal-scoring charts as a returning player (after time at UCD and Fleetwood Town) suggests a significant and measurable improvement in output back in the League of Ireland.
evidence.notes: The full article could not be fetched (access denied); this claim is based on the headline/search-summary only, and exact month and goal tally are not confirmed.

evidence.claim: Noah Jauny, born in Dublin to an Irish mother and French former-footballer father, is dual-eligible for Ireland and France but has consistently chosen to represent Ireland, rejecting suggestions of a switch to France.
evidence.interpretation: A clear, repeated public commitment to Ireland despite equally valid French eligibility removes ambiguity about his international allegiance, distinguishing him from merely 'potentially eligible' dual-nationality prospects.

evidence.claim: Noah Jauny left Ligue 1 club Stade Brestois for Belgian second-tier club Francs Borains, reported as being in search of regular playing time after failing to break through at Brest.
evidence.interpretation: A move down from a Ligue 1 club to a second-tier Belgian club, explicitly framed as being about seeking playing time, suggests his development had stalled at his previous club.

evidence.claim: Franco Umeh-Chibueze made his Portsmouth debut on 29 December 2025 in a 2-1 win over Charlton Athletic at Fratton Park, more than four months after signing permanently from Crystal Palace, having been delayed by a hamstring injury.
evidence.interpretation: A debut delayed significantly by injury after a permanent transfer means his true first-team integration only began in very late 2025, so any 2026 progression should be judged from that later starting point rather than from his transfer date.

evidence.claim: Seán Grehan has won eight caps for the Republic of Ireland U21s, including captaining the side in a friendly against Croatia, and signed a permanent three-year deal with Doncaster Rovers (EFL League One) from Crystal Palace in June 2025.
evidence.interpretation: Being trusted with the U21 captaincy alongside a permanent move to a settled League One club suggests a player valued for leadership and consistency rather than being an unproven fringe prospect.

evidence.claim: Adam Brennan, who signed for Shamrock Rovers from UCD on 30 January 2026, received his first Republic of Ireland U21 call-up ahead of the March 2026 Euro qualifiers against Moldova and Kazakhstan.
evidence.interpretation: A first U21 call-up arriving within roughly two months of joining a bigger League of Ireland club suggests the move to Shamrock Rovers coincided with, or helped prompt, international recognition.

evidence.claim: Aarón Ochoa Moloney made his Republic of Ireland U21 debut as a starter in a 1-0 win over Kazakhstan in UEFA U21 Euro qualifying on 31 March 2026, having received his first U21 call-up that March.
evidence.interpretation: Going straight into the starting line-up on debut, rather than appearing as a substitute, indicates the U21 coaching staff had strong confidence in him immediately.

evidence.claim: Sean Patton scored five goals in six games during a loan spell at National League club Aldershot Town before being recalled by Reading, subsequently making his first senior league start for Reading in a 2-1 win over Burton Albion.
evidence.interpretation: A high scoring rate on loan followed by an immediate recall and first-team debut is a fairly clear marker of a successful loan directly translating into first-team opportunity at the parent club.

evidence.claim: John O'Sullivan (born 29 January 2006) made his Republic of Ireland U19 debut on 5 September 2024 and was named in the FAI's 1 June 2026 U21 squad for the Croatia/Qatar friendlies.
evidence.interpretation: Progression from U19 debut to U21 squad inclusion within roughly 21 months is a normal, positive age-grade progression, though squad inclusion does not confirm he actually played for the U21s.

evidence.claim: Cory O'Sullivan received his first Republic of Ireland U21 call-up on 21 May 2025 and made his U21 debut on 10 June 2025 in a 0-0 draw with Qatar U23, having previously progressed through Ireland's U17 and U19 sides.
evidence.interpretation: A steady progression through U17, U19 and into U21 international football over consecutive years indicates a consistent development pathway recognised at each age grade.
